rubrics.rationale: The core workflows work end to end. The app generates a 5-color palette in 9 harmony modes, takes a seed color from a picker or HEX input, locks colors and blocks generation when all are locked. It copies HEX/RGB/HSL, exports CSS, Tailwind, JSON and SVG, saves, reloads, deletes and clears palettes, and shares a link. Privacy and terms pages, SEO content, the FAQ and the Pro note are present, and next build produced static routes. Several requested behaviors are missing or changed. There is no Randomize button and no subheading text. Cards show only the best text color and a ratio with AA/AAA. They do not show contrast against both black and white or the 'Good for text'/'Use carefully'/'Decorative only' labels. Share URLs use '-' separators, so the requested comma format is rejected. A malformed URL rejects the whole palette instead of ignoring only the invalid colors. Saving a duplicate does not show 'Already saved'. The empty-state text differs from the requested copy.

The project uses the requested stack: Next.js App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind and localStorage. There is no backend, auth, database or external API, and the file layout mostly matches the request. Storage, clipboard and URL errors show a visible message. However, every dependency is pinned to 'latest', and the build pulled a Next.js 16 canary. A lint script is declared, but the project has no ESLint config file. The share URL format was changed from the requested comma format without saying so.

Each locked feature has a deterministic verify command backed by vitest test files. The verify script also enforces a 500-line limit on lib modules. The PR records hold tool-captured exit code 0 with output tails, including a full next build route table, plus a no-fallback hook scan and line counts. Lint and type-check are not part of the verify chain, and the vitest config warning was not addressed.

Labeled inputs, the mode select, the primary Generate button, an aria-live notice region, focus-visible outlines, aria-pressed on lock and format toggles, and descriptive aria-labels on icon buttons give a clear, keyboard-usable workflow. Weaknesses include icon-only visible lock state, hidden RGB and HSL values below sm, very small text, a missing hero subheading, and AA/AAA jargon rather than plain-language guidance.

Untrusted input is validated. Stored JSON uses a type guard, and JSON-LD escapes '<'. Failures surface explicitly. Modules are small and cohesive. Risks include floating latest dependencies and client components relying on inheritance of the client boundary.
